headline: Nvidia launches RTX Spark mini desktops for local AI
dek: According to Nvidia, compact PCs from Asus, Dell and MSI run agents and models without the cloud.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What was announced
body: Nvidia announced the RTX Spark compact desktops, built by Asus, Dell and MSI and on sale since November 18 (NVIDIA).
They run AI agents, generate images and video and fine-tune models on the machine itself, the company says (NVIDIA).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: The hardware
s3.body: According to Nvidia, each machine pairs its own CPU and GPU.

points.t: A 20-core Grace chip, per the company (NVIDIA).
Up to 1 petaflop of AI performance (NVIDIA).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why run AI locally
body: Nvidia says local models avoid per-token charges and keep code and files on the machine (NVIDIA).
A feature called Switchyard decides what runs locally and what goes to the cloud (NVIDIA).

items.t: Native Windows on Arm support in Photoshop and Premiere (NVIDIA).

caption.hook: Nvidia launches RTX Spark mini desktops to run AI locally.
body: According to a Nvidia statement, the RTX Spark compact desktops, built by Asus, Dell and MSI, have been on sale since November 18 (NVIDIA). The company says they run AI agents, generate images and video and fine-tune models without the cloud, with a 20-core Grace CPU and up to 128GB of unified memory.

Nvidia says running models locally avoids per-token charges and keeps code and files on the machine, and a feature called Switchyard decides what stays local and what goes to the cloud (NVIDIA). It also cites native Adobe support for Windows on Arm and integration with Blender and ComfyUI.
